submission.justification: Sensor-T3 is excluded: its measured hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2 is 82.0% (charge trapping, full depletion unreachable), far below the hard 97% requirement. Of the remaining candidates, Sensor-T1 and Sensor-T2 both pass efficiency (98.5% and 99.2% at 2e16). T2 resolution is worse at every thickness simulated (about 14-16 um vs. about 9 um for T1). For T1, a thickness scan (unirradiated) gave: 50 um 10.32, 100 um 9.27, 125 um 9.09, 150 um 8.68, 175 um 8.86, 200 um 9.22 um. The minimum is at 150 um, giving the best single-hit resolution of the options that meet the constraints. Caveats: the simulation is unirradiated, and the irradiation campaign does not state the thickness of the tested T1 sensors, so the 98.5% efficiency is taken as applying to a 150 um T1 sensor. This should be confirmed with a 150 um irradiated test if possible.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three candidate technologies
Hit efficiency >= 97% up to 2e16 neq/cm^2 (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: irradiation_testbeam_2026.md: Sensor-T1 98.5% at 2e16 neq/cm^2. Thickness of the tested sample is not stated, so applicability to 150 um is an assumption to confirm.

requirements.requirement: Best possible single-hit spatial resolution in innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Simulated unirradiated resolution: T1 at 150 um = 8.68 um, the minimum of the T1 scan (50-200 um). T2 best ~13.9 um (150 um); T3 has the best unirradiated resolution (6.0 um at 150 um, 2025 summary) but fails efficiency.
